title: Arakhin 22
description: How long the sale of orphans’ property is proclaimed, and whether the court sells minor orphans’ property to pay their father’s debts at all: Rav Asi and Rabbi Yoḥanan, the gentile creditor, the marriage contract “for the sake of favor”, the reasons for waiting until the orphans grow up, and when a steward is appointed.
topics: 📣 Thirty days or sixty: Rabbi Meir, Rabbi Yehuda and the Rabbis on proclaiming the sale
📅 Avimi’s blows: thirty consecutive days, or sixty days of Mondays and Thursdays
💸 Rav Asi and Rabbi Yoḥanan: the court sells orphans’ property only against interest, or also for a widow’s marriage contract
🤝 The gentile creditor who accepted Jewish law for this, but not for that
💍 A marriage contract “for the sake of favor”: Mareimar collects for a divorcée
👛 Why wait until the orphans grow up? Rav Pappa’s mitzva, Rav Huna son of Rav Yehoshua’s bundles, Rava’s receipt
🧾 “Give this field” or “give a field”: Rava, the Sages of Neharde’a and Rav Ashi on appointing a steward

a1.he: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: שׁוּם הַיְּתוֹמִים שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, וְשׁוּם הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ שִׁשִּׁים יוֹם, דִּבְרֵי רַבִּי מֵאִיר. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: שׁוּם הַיְּתוֹמִים שִׁשִּׁים יוֹם, וְשׁוּם הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ תִּשְׁעִים יוֹם. וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: אֶחָד זֶה וְאֶחָד זֶה שִׁשִּׁים יוֹם. אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא אָמַר אֲבִימִי: הֲלָכָה שׁוּם הַיְּתוֹמִים שִׁשִּׁים יוֹם.

a2.he: יָתֵיב רַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין וְקָאָמַר לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק לְרַבִּי חִיָּיא בַּר אָבִין: שִׁשִּׁים קָאָמְרַתְּ אוֹ שְׁלֹשִׁים קָאָמְרַתְּ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: שִׁשִּׁים. דִּיתוֹמִים אוֹ דְּהֶקְדֵּשׁ? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: דִּיתוֹמִים.

a3.he: כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר אוֹ כְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה? אֲמַר לֵיהּ: כְּרַבִּי מֵאִיר, וְהָא רַבִּי מֵאִיר שְׁלֹשִׁים קָאָמַר!

a4.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָכִי אָמַר רַב חִסְדָּא: מֵאֲבִימִי קוּלְפֵי טָאבֵי בְּלַעִי עֲלַהּ דְּהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא, בָּא לְהַכְרִיז רְצוּפִים — שְׁלֹשִׁים.

a5.he: בְּשֵׁנִי וּבַחֲמִישִׁי, שִׁשִּׁים, וְאַף עַל גַּב דְּכִי חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ מָר לְיוֹמֵי הַכְרָזָה לָא הָווּ אֶלָּא תְּמָנֵיסַר יוֹמֵי, כֵּיוָן דְּמָשְׁכָא מִילְּתָא שָׁמְעִי אִינָשֵׁי.

a6.he: אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: אֵין נִזְקָקִין לְנִכְסֵי יְתוֹמִים, אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיְתָה רִבִּית אוֹכֶלֶת בָּהֶן. וְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אוֹמֵר: אוֹ לִשְׁטָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ רִבִּית, אוֹ לִכְתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה מִשּׁוּם מְזוֹנֵי.

a7.he: וְרַב אַסִּי מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר לִכְתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה? דְּהָא תַּקִּינוּ לֵיה רַבָּנַן מַעֲשֵׂה יָדֶיהָ, וְאִידַּךְ? זִימְנִין דְּלָא סָפְקָה.

a8.he: תְּנַן: שׁוּם הַיְּתוֹמִים שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, וְשׁוּם הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ שִׁשִּׁים יוֹם, וּמַכְרִיזִין בַּבֹּקֶר וּבָעֶרֶב. בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בְּבַעַל חוֹב גּוֹי, מִי צָיֵית? אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּבַעַל חוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל. אִי דְּקָאָכֵיל רִיבִּיתָא, מִי שָׁבְקִינַן לֵיהּ? וְאֶלָּא דְּלָא קָאָכֵיל רִיבִּיתָא, וְקָתָנֵי: נִזְקָקִין!

a9.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מוֹקֵי לַהּ בִּכְתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה, אֶלָּא לְרַב אַסִּי קַשְׁיָא. אָמַר לְךָ רַב אַסִּי: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִי נִיחָא? מִי שָׁבְקִינַן מְזוֹנֵי דְּוַדַּאי קָא מַפְסְדָא, וְנָקְטִינַן הַכְרָזָה דְּלָא יָדְעִינַן אִי מַרְוְוחִינַן אִי לָא מַרְוְוחִינַן?

a10.he: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, בְּתוֹבַעַת כְּתוּבָּתָהּ בְּבֵית דִּין, כִּדְרַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל, דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל: הַתּוֹבַעַת כְּתוּבָּתָהּ בְּבֵית דִּין אֵין לָהּ מְזוֹנוֹת.

a11.he: אִי הָכִי, אִיזְדְּקוֹקֵי לָא מִיזְדַּקְקִינַן לַהּ, אֶלָּא כֵּיוָן דְּאִיזְדַּקְקִינַן לַהּ מֵעִיקָּרָא, מִיזְדַּקְקִינַן לַהּ לְבַסּוֹף.

a12.he: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם, לְרַב אַסִּי קַשְׁיָא! לְעוֹלָם בְּבַעַל חוֹב גּוֹי, שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו לָדוּן בְּדִינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.

a13.he: אִי הָכִי, רִבִּית נָמֵי לָא לִישְׁקוֹל! שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו לָזוֹ, וְלֹא קִיבֵּל עָלָיו לָזוֹ.

a14.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: ״אֵין נִפְרָעִין מִנִּכְסֵי יְתוֹמִים אֶלָּא מִן הַזִּיבּוּרִית״. בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בְּבַעַל חוֹב גּוֹי — מִי צָאֵית? אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּבַעַל חוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל. אִי אָכֵיל רִיבִּיתָא — מִי שָׁבְקִינַן לֵיהּ? אֶלָּא דְּלָא אָכֵיל רִיבִּיתָא, וְקָתָנֵי: נִזְקָקִין!

a15.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן, מוֹקֵי לַהּ בִּכְתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה, אֶלָּא לְרַב אַסִּי קַשְׁיָא. אָמַר לְךָ רַב אַסִּי: וּלְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִי נִיחָא? אִי כְּתוּבָּה, מַאי אִירְיָא מִיַּתְמֵי? אֲפִילּוּ מִינֵּיהּ דִּידֵיהּ נָמֵי בְּזִיבּוּרִית!

a16.he: הָא לָא קַשְׁיָא, רַבִּי מֵאִיר הִיא, דְּאָמַר: כְּתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה בְּבֵינוֹנִית, וּמִיַּתְמֵי בְּזִיבּוּרִית.

a17.he: מִכׇּל מָקוֹם, לְרַב אַסִּי קַשְׁיָא! לְעוֹלָם בְּבַעַל חוֹב גּוֹי, שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו לָדוּן בְּדִינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל. אִי הָכִי, רִבִּית נָמֵי לָא נִישְׁקוֹל! שֶׁקִּיבֵּל לְזוֹ, וְלֹא קִיבֵּל עָלָיו לָזוֹ.

a18.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: עַל מְנָת לִיתֵּן לָאִשָּׁה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ וּלְבַעַל חוֹב חוֹבוֹ. בִּשְׁלָמָא בַּעַל חוֹב, בֵּין מָר וּבֵין מָר — כִּדְשַׁנִּין.

a19.he: אֶלָּא כְּתוּבָּתָהּ, בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן נִיחָא, אֶלָּא לְרַב אַסִּי קַשְׁיָא!

a20.he: הָכָא בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן — כְּשֶׁחַיָּיב מוֹדֶה. הַשְׁתָּא דְּאָתֵית לְהָכִי, כּוּלְּהוּ נָמֵי כְּשֶׁחַיָּיב מוֹדֶה.

a21.he: מָרִימָר אַגְבֵּי (כתובתה) [כְּתוּבָּה] לִגְרוּשָׁה מִנִּכְסֵי דְּיַתְמֵי. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְאַמֵּימָר: וְהָאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר רַב אַסִּי: ״אֵין נִזְקָקִין לְנִכְסֵי יְתוֹמִין אֶלָּא אִם כֵּן הָיְתָה רִבִּית אוֹכֶלֶת בָּהֶן״. רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן אוֹמֵר: אוֹ לִשְׁטָר שֶׁיֵּשׁ בּוֹ רִבִּית, אוֹ לִכְתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה מִשּׁוּם מְזוֹנֵי!

a22.he: וַאֲפִילּוּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לָא קָאָמַר אֶלָּא בְּאַלְמָנָה, דְּקָמַפְסְדָא מְזוֹנֵי, אֲבָל גְּרוּשָׁה לָא!

a23.he: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא אֲנַן דְּרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן מִשּׁוּם חִינָּא מַתְנִינַן לַהּ.

a24.he: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: מֵרֵישָׁא לָא הֲוָה מִיזְדְּקִיקְנָא לְנִכְסֵי יַתְמֵי, כֵּיוָן דִּשְׁמַעְנָא לְהָא דְּרַב הוּנָא חַבְרִין מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּרַב: ״יַתְמֵי דְּאָכְלִי דְּלָא דִּידְהוּ לֵיזְלוּ בָּתַר שִׁיבְקַיְיהוּ״, מִכָּאן וְאֵילָךְ מִיזְדְּקִקְנָא.

a25.he: מֵעִיקָּרָא מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: פְּרִיעַת בַּעַל חוֹב מִצְוָה, וְיַתְמֵי לָא בְּנֵי מֶיעְבַּד מִצְוָה נִינְהוּ. רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר: אֵימַר צְרָרֵי אַתְפְּסֵיהּ.

a26.he: מַאי בֵּינַיְיהוּ? אִיכָּא בֵּינַיְיהוּ בְּשֶׁחַיָּיב מוֹדֶה, אִי נָמֵי שַׁמְּתוּהּ וּמִית בְּשַׁמְתֵּיהּ.

a27.he: שְׁלַחוּ מִתָּם, דְּשַׁמְּתוּהּ וּמִית בְּשַׁמְתֵּיהּ, וְהִלְכְתָא כְּרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ.

b1.he: תְּנַן: שׁוּם הַיְּתוֹמִים שְׁלֹשִׁים יוֹם, וְשׁוּם הַהֶקְדֵּשׁ שִׁשִּׁים יוֹם, וּמַכְרִיזִין בַּבֹּקֶר וּבָעֶרֶב. בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בְּבַעַל חוֹב גּוֹי — מִי צָאֵית? אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּבַעַל חוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל.

b2.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, מוֹקֵי לַהּ בְּשֶׁחַיָּיב מוֹדֶה, אֶלָּא לְרַב פָּפָּא — קַשְׁיָא!

b3.he: אָמַר לְךָ רַב פָּפָּא: אִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא — כְּתוּבָּה מִשּׁוּם חִינָּא, וְאִי בָּעֵית אֵימָא — בְּבַעַל חוֹב גּוֹי שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו לָדוּן בְּדִינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל.

b4.he: אִי קִיבֵּל עָלָיו, לִינְטַר לְהוּ עַד דְּגָדְלִי! שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו לָזוֹ, וְלֹא קִיבֵּל עָלָיו לָזוֹ.

b5.he: תָּא שְׁמַע: עַל מְנָת לִיתֵּן לָאִשָּׁה כְּתוּבָּתָהּ, וּלְבַעַל חוֹב חוֹבוֹ. בְּמַאי עָסְקִינַן? אִילֵימָא בְּבַעַל חוֹב גּוֹי — מִי צָיֵית? אֶלָּא פְּשִׁיטָא בְּבַעַל חוֹב יִשְׂרָאֵל.

b6.he: בִּשְׁלָמָא לְרַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, מוֹקֵי לַהּ בְּשֶׁחַיָּיב מוֹדֶה. אֶלָּא לְרַב פָּפָּא, בִּשְׁלָמָא כְּתוּבָּה — מִשּׁוּם חִינָּא, אֶלָּא בַּעַל חוֹב קַשְׁיָא!

b7.he: לְעוֹלָם בְּבַעַל חוֹב גּוֹי, וּכְגוֹן שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו לָדוּן בְּדִינֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל. אִי קִיבֵּל עָלָיו, לִינְטַר לְהוּ עַד דְּגָדְלִי! שֶׁקִּיבֵּל עָלָיו לָזוֹ, וְלֹא קִיבֵּל עָלָיו לָזוֹ.

b8.he: רָבָא אָמַר: מִשּׁוּם שׁוֹבָר. אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ לְרָבָא: וּמִי חָיְישִׁינַן לְשׁוֹבָר? וְהָתְנַן: הַנִּפְרַעַת שֶׁלֹּא בְּפָנָיו — לֹא תִּפָּרַע אֶלָּא בִּשְׁבוּעָה.

b9.he: וְאָמַר רַבִּי אַחָא שַׂר הַבִּירָה: מַעֲשֶׂה בָּא לִפְנֵי רַבִּי יִצְחָק נַפָּחָא לְאַנְטוֹכְיָא, וְאָמַר: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא כְּתוּבַּת אִשָּׁה מִשּׁוּם חִינָּא, אֲבָל בַּעַל חוֹב — לָא, וְרַבָּה אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן: אֲפִילּוּ בַּעַל חוֹב נָמֵי,

b10.he: וְאִי חָיְישַׁתְּ לְשׁוֹבָר — הָתָם נָמֵי נֵיחוּשׁ! אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָתָם, כִּדְאָמְרִינַן טַעְמָא, שֶׁלֹּא יְהֵא כׇּל אֶחָד נוֹטֵל מְעוֹתָיו שֶׁל חֲבֵירוֹ וְהוֹלֵךְ וְיוֹשֵׁב לוֹ בִּמְדִינַת הַיָּם.

b11.he: אָמַר רָבָא, הִלְכְתָא: אֵין נִזְקָקִין לְנִכְסֵי יְתוֹמִין, וְאִם אָמַר: ״תְּנוּ״ — נִזְקָקִין. ״שָׂדֶה זוֹ״ וּ״מָנֶה זוֹ״ — נִזְקָקִין וְאֵין מַעֲמִידִין אַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס, ״שָׂדֶה״ סְתָם וּ״מָנֶה״ סְתָם — נִזְקָקִין וּמַעֲמִידִין אַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס.

b12.he: אָמְרִי נְהַרְדָּעֵי: בְּכוּלְּהוּ נִזְקָקִין וּמַעֲמִידִין אַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס, לְבַד מִנִּמְצֵאת שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁלּוֹ, דְּאַחְזוֹקֵי סָהֲדֵי בְּשַׁקָּרֵי לָא מַחְזְקִינַן.

b13.he: אָמַר רַב אָשֵׁי: הִלְכָּךְ אִזְדְּקוֹקֵי לָא מִזְדַּקְקִינַן, דְּהָא אָמַר רָבָא: הִלְכְתָא אֵין נִזְקָקִין, וְאִי מִזְדַּקְקִינַן מוֹקְמִינַן אַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס, דְּאָמְרִי נְהַרְדָּעֵי: בְּכוּלְּהוּ נִזְקָקִין וּמַעֲמִידִין אַפּוֹטְרוֹפּוֹס, לְבַד מִנִּמְצֵאת שָׂדֶה שֶׁאֵינָהּ שֶׁלּוֹ, דְּאַחְזוֹקֵי סָהֲדֵי בְּשַׁקָּרֵי לָא מַחְזְקִינַן.

messages.text: Continued from 21b: Chapter 6, Shum HaYetomim, opened with the mishna: the appraisal of orphans’ property is proclaimed for thirty days and that of consecrated property for sixty days, in the morning and in the evening. A baraita gave the wording of the proclamation, which says the field is sold to pay a wife’s marriage contract or a creditor’s debt.
One proclaims the appraisal of the property inherited by minor orphans for thirty days, and one proclaims the appraisal of consecrated property for sixty days. This is the statement of Rabbi Meir.
messages.lead: With regard to the duration of time for the proclamation, the Sages taught:

messages.text: One proclaims the appraisal of the property of orphans for sixty days, and one proclaims the appraisal of consecrated property for ninety days.
Both this and that are proclaimed for sixty days.
The halakha is that one proclaims the appraisal of the property of orphans for sixty days.
Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin was sitting and saying this halakha stated by Rav Ḥisda in the name of Avimi.

notes.he: דרב חסדא:
notes.en: This teaching: Rav Ḥisda’s.

messages.text: Did you say that the proclamation is for sixty days or did you say that it is for thirty days?
messages.lead: Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak said to Rabbi Ḥiyya bar Avin:

messages.text: It is for sixty days.
Is this the halakha with regard to the property of orphans or with regard to consecrated property?
It applies to the property of orphans.
Do you rule in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir or in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Yehuda?
I rule in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir.
But Rabbi Meir says that the appraisal of the property of orphans is proclaimed for thirty days.
messages.quote: thirty days … the statement of Rabbi Meir

messages.text: I absorbed many blows [kulfei] from Avimi due to that halakha, i.e., Avimi would disparage me when I questioned his statement that according to Rabbi Meir one proclaims the appraisal of the property of orphans for sixty days, which is contradicted by the baraita.

notes.he: הכאות גדולות על הדא שמעתא שהיה מלמדיני שום היתומים לרבי מאיר ששים יום והייתי מקשה לו הא אמר ר"מ שלשים והוא אמר לי בא להכריז רצופין שלשים יום בין יתומין בין הקדש:
notes.en: Kulfei tavei: great blows, over this teaching. For he would teach me that the appraisal of orphans’ property, according to Rabbi Meir, is sixty days, and I would object to him: But Rabbi Meir said thirty! And he said to me: If he comes to proclaim on consecutive days, it is thirty days, whether for orphans or for consecrated property.

notes.he: מכות טובות קבלתי מאבימי רבי קודם שהבנתי שמועה זו:
notes.en: Kulfei tavei: good blows I received from Avimi my teacher before I understood this teaching.

messages.text: @Rav Ḥisda If the court comes to proclaim the sale on consecutive days, then it is proclaimed for thirty days, in accordance with the baraita.

notes.he: [והכי אמר לי בא להכריז רצופין בכל יום ויום אינו צריך להכריז אלא שלשים אבל אם אינו מכריז אלא בשני ובחמישי צריך להכריז בב' ובה' של ס' יום:
notes.en: And so he said to me: If he comes to proclaim consecutively, on every single day, he need proclaim only thirty; but if he proclaims only on Mondays and Thursdays, he must proclaim on the Mondays and Thursdays of sixty days.

messages.text: But if it is proclaimed only on Monday and on Thursday, when the markets are open, villagers gather in the city, and the courts sit in judgment, then it is proclaimed over the course of sixty days.

notes.he: שהם ימי הדין הוי השום ששים יום וימי הכרזה שמונה עשר יום צא וחשוב משני בשבת שמונה שבועות הרי לך נ"ו ימים ויהא בהם י"ו שני חמישי הוסיף עוד ארבעה ימים שני ושלישי ורביעי וחמישי בשבת הרי ס' יום משהתחיל ההכרזה ויש בהן שמונה עשר ימי הכרזה:
notes.en: And if he comes to proclaim on Mondays and Thursdays, which are the days of judgment, the appraisal is sixty days, and the days of proclamation are eighteen. Go and count eight weeks from a Monday: that gives you fifty-six days, and they contain sixteen Mondays and Thursdays. Add four more days, Monday, Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday: that makes sixty days from when the proclamation began, and they contain eighteen days of proclamation.

messages.text: And even though if Master counts the number of days on which there is actually a proclamation, there are only eighteen days, far fewer than the thirty of the consecutive days, since the matter extends over the course of sixty days, people will hear about the sale.

notes.he: לא הוו אלא י"ח יום הכי כיצד כשתתחיל למנות מיום שני ס' יום הם ח' שבועות וד' ימים וח' שבועות ט"ז ימי הכרזה ואותן ד' ימים מתחילין ביום שני ומסיימין בחמישי היינו תמניסר:
notes.en: And even though when you count them there are only eighteen days: how so? When you begin counting sixty days from a Monday, they are eight weeks and four days. Eight weeks have sixteen days of proclamation, and those four days begin on a Monday and end on a Thursday: that makes eighteen.

notes.he: דהני תמניסר עד ס' יום שמעי אינשי]:
notes.en: Since the matter extends: since these eighteen stretch over sixty days, people hear.

messages.caption: Sixty days of Mondays and Thursdays hold eighteen days of proclamation, counted as Rashi and Rabbeinu Gershom count them.

messages.text: § The court attends to the property of minor orphans, to sell it in order to pay a debt, only if the debt was accruing interest that consumes the property of the orphans, since if they delay payment of the debt, it will grow dramatically. In other cases the court delays payment until the orphans reach majority.

notes.he: למוכרן:
notes.en: One does not attend to the property of orphans: to sell it.

notes.he: שהיו מחוייבין לעובד כוכבים מעות ברבית:
notes.en: Interest consuming it: they owed money at interest to a gentile.

notes.he: אין נזקקין לנכסי יתומין כשהן קטנים אבל כי גדלי ודאי נזקקין למוכרן לפרוע:
notes.en: One does not attend to the property of orphans while they are minors; but when they grow up, certainly one attends to selling it in order to pay.

notes.he: שזקף אביהן מלוה ברבית ומפסידים היתומים בכל יום:
notes.en: Unless interest is consuming it: their father had taken a loan at interest, and the orphans lose every day.

messages.text: The court attends to their property either to pay a debt recorded in a promissory note that contains interest or to pay a wife’s marriage contract, due to the standing obligation of the orphans to provide sustenance for their father’s widow from his estate as long as she has not received payment of her marriage contract. It is therefore beneficial to the orphans that she should collect her marriage contract immediately.

notes.he: דכל זמן שאינה גובה כתובתה נזונית משלהם והוי פסידא דידהו:
notes.en: Because of sustenance: for as long as she has not collected her marriage contract she is sustained from their property, and that is a loss to them.

notes.he: לפרוע כתובת אשת אביהן שכל זמן שלא גבתה כתובה ניזונת מן היתומים ומפסידי מזונות]:
notes.en: Or for a wife’s marriage contract because of sustenance: to pay the marriage contract of their father’s wife, for as long as she has not collected her marriage contract she is sustained from the orphans, and they lose the sustenance.

messages.text: And Rav Asi, what is the reason that he did not state that the court attends to their property for the purpose of paying the marriage contract of a wife?
messages.quote: a wife’s marriage contract, due to the standing obligation of the orphans to provide sustenance

messages.text: There is no financial loss to the orphans in such a case, because the Sages established for the late husband that as long as she receives sustenance from his estate, the orphans are entitled to her earnings.

notes.he: ליתמי מעשי ידי אשת אביהן להן הואיל וניזונת משלהן ואין להן הפסד במזונות:
notes.en: For they established for them: [the Sages gave] the orphans the earnings of their father’s wife, since she is sustained from theirs, and so they have no loss from the sustenance.

messages.text: And the other, Rabbi Yoḥanan, in light of this fact why does he rule that the court attends to their property?
Sometimes her earnings do not provide enough to reimburse the money spent on her sustenance.

notes.he: משום הכי נזקקין לכתובה משום דזימנין דלא ספקה מלאכת' כנגד מזונותיה ונפסדין היתומין:
notes.en: And Rabbi Yoḥanan says: for this reason one attends to the marriage contract, because sometimes her work does not match her sustenance, and the orphans lose.

messages.text: We learned in the mishna:
One proclaims the appraisal of the property inherited by orphans for thirty days and the appraisal of consecrated property for sixty days, and one proclaims it in the morning and in the evening.
What case are we dealing with in the mishna? If we say that we are dealing with a gentile creditor, will he comply with the ruling of the Jewish court that payment be delayed for thirty days?

notes.he: דשקיל רבית ולהכי נזקקין:
notes.en: If we say with a gentile creditor: who takes interest, and that is why one attends.

notes.he: להמתין ימי הכרזתינו בלא רבית:
notes.en: Will he comply: and wait the days of our proclamation without interest?

notes.dh: תנן שום היתומים כו' במאי עסקינן אלימא בבעל חוב עובד כוכבים מי ציית
notes.he: ואם תאמר למה ליה לאותובי לרב אסי ממתניתין ממילתיה דרב אסי גופיה הוה מצי למיפרך דאמר דאין נזקקין לנכסי יתומים אלא אם כן רבית אוכלת בהם במאי עסקינן האי דאין נזקקין אילימא בבעל חוב עובד כוכבים מי ציית להמתין עד שיגדילו ואי בבעל חוב ישראל מי שבקינן ליה דקאכיל רבית וי"ל דממילתא דרב אסי לא מצי למיפרך דאפשר לאוקמה בדלא תבע להו ולעולם בב"ח עובד כוכבים איירי ומש"ה אין נזקקין לנכסים לפרוע החוב אלא אם כן רבית אוכלת בהן [ואז] נזקקין אפי' לא תבע להו עובד כוכבים חובו לפי שלא ירבה עליהן הרבית אבל ממתניתין פריך שפיר דודאי מדנחתי בית דין לשום בדתבע להו מיירי לפיכך פריך אי בבעל חוב עובד כוכבים מי ציית עד אחר השלמת הכרזה שלא להרבות הרבית ואי לא ציית אם כן שמא יפסידו בהארכת הזמן יותר ממה שירויחו דודאי אי לא ידעינן אי מרווחינן אי לא מרווחינן לא צריכי הכרזה כדקאמר הש"ס בסמוך על מילתא דר' יוחנן:
notes.en: We learned: the appraisal of orphans, etc. What are we dealing with? If we say with a gentile creditor, will he comply? And if you will say: why does it need to object to Rav Asi from our mishna? It could have objected from Rav Asi’s own statement, where he said that one does not attend to the property of orphans unless interest is consuming it: what are we dealing with in this “one does not attend”? If we say with a gentile creditor, will he comply and wait until they grow up? And if with a Jewish creditor, do we let him consume interest? One can say: from Rav Asi’s statement it could not object, since it can be established where [the creditor] did not claim from them, and it really speaks of a gentile creditor. That is why one does not attend to the property to pay the debt unless interest is consuming it; [then] one attends even if the gentile did not claim his debt from them, so that the interest will not grow upon them. But from our mishna it objects well, since certainly, from the fact that the court goes down to appraise, it speaks of where he claimed from them. Therefore it objects: if with a gentile creditor, will he comply until after the proclamation is completed, so as not to increase the interest? And if he will not comply, then perhaps they will lose more by the extension of time than they will gain; for certainly, if we do not know whether we gain or not, they would not need a proclamation, as the Talmud says shortly about Rabbi Yoḥanan’s statement.

notes.he: כדי לפרוע לב"ח פרסי מי צאית פרסי להמתין עד שנכריז שלשים:
notes.en: If we say: in order to pay a Persian creditor [Rabbeinu Gershom reads “Persian” where the Davidson English has “gentile”], will a Persian comply and wait until we proclaim for thirty [days]?

messages.text: Rather, it is obvious that we are dealing with a Jewish creditor. Now, if the mishna is dealing with a situation where the interest consumes the orphans’ property, do we leave a Jew to collect interest?

notes.he: מן היתומין כלומר דמשום הכי נזקקין מי שבקינן ליה לב"ח ישראל למשקל רבית:
notes.en: And if he is consuming interest from the orphans, that is, that this is why one attends: do we let a Jewish creditor take interest?

messages.text: But rather, it must be referring to a case where the interest does not consume the orphans’ property, and nevertheless the mishna teaches that the court attends to the property of orphans even when no interest accrues on the loan. This apparently contradicts the opinions of Rav Asi and Rabbi Yoḥanan.

Granted, according to the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan the mishna is not difficult, as he can establish it as referring to payment of the marriage contract of a wife. But according to the opinion of Rav Asi, that the court does not attend to the property of orphans in such a case, the mishna poses a difficulty.

notes.he: ולהכי נזקקין דקא מפסידי מזוני:
notes.en: He establishes it with a wife’s marriage contract: and that is why one attends, since they lose sustenance.

notes.he: אמאי נזקקין למכור הא אין רבית איכא בהן]:
notes.en: But according to Rav Asi: why does one attend to selling? There is no interest here!

messages.text: Rav Asi could say to you: And according to the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, does it work out well that the mishna requires thirty days of proclamation before the sale of the property?

Do we leave aside the sustenance that the orphans certainly lose to the wife for the duration of the thirty days and take, i.e., implement, the proclamation, with regard to which we do not know if they will gain from it or if they will not gain, as it is uncertain that an offer matching the appraisal of the court will be made?

notes.he: אמאי מכריזין יתנו כתובתה לאלתר ותסתלק ממזונות השתא שבקינן לה למיכל מזוני דודאי קא מפסדי עד שיגמרו ימי הכרזה ונקטינן הכרזה דלא ידעינן אי מרווחנא ליתמי [אי לא] ספק הוא אם יוסיפו על השומא [כלום] אי לא:
notes.en: And according to Rabbi Yoḥanan, does it work out? Why proclaim? Let them give her marriage contract at once, and she will be removed from sustenance. Now we let her consume sustenance, which is certainly a loss until the days of proclamation end, and we take the proclamation, about which we do not know whether we gain for the orphans or not: it is uncertain whether they will add anything to the appraisal or not.

messages.text: This is not difficult, as Rabbi Yoḥanan can explain that the mishna is referring to a widow who claims her marriage contract in court. And this is in accordance with a ruling that Rav Yehuda says that Shmuel says,

notes.he: דכיון דשוב אין לה מזונות לא מפסדי יתומים מידי בהמתנה:
notes.en: With one who claims her marriage contract in court: since she then no longer has sustenance, the orphans lose nothing by waiting.

notes.he: [אמר לך ר' יוחנן הא לא קשיא מאי דאמרת שבקינן לה למיכל מזוני דקא מפסדא דבתובעת כתובתה בב"ד עסקינן דאין לה מזונות:
notes.en: Rabbi Yoḥanan could say to you: This is not difficult. As for what you said, that we let her consume sustenance, which is a loss: we are dealing with one who claims her marriage contract in court, who has no sustenance.

messages.text: A widow who claims payment of her marriage contract in court no longer receives sustenance from the estate of her husband.

If so, then we should not attend to her request to collect payment of her marriage contract at all. Rather, the court should delay payment until the orphans reach majority, as they incur no loss by delaying the payment.

notes.he: לפרוע כתובתה הואיל ומעכשיו אין מזונותיה על היתומים:
notes.en: We should not attend to her: to pay her marriage contract, since from now on her sustenance is no longer upon the orphans.

notes.he: דבתובעת כתובתה בב"ד עסקינן איזדקוקי נמי לא איזדקיק לה לא למכור ולא להכריז הואיל וכבר איבדה מזונותיה:
notes.en: If so, that we are dealing with one who claims her marriage contract in court, we should not attend to her at all, neither to sell nor to proclaim, since she has already lost her sustenance.

messages.text: That is not appropriate; rather, since we attend to her initially, when she claims the payment of her marriage contract in court, we attend to her in the end as well, in order to collect payment from the orphans, despite the fact that the orphans will not lose money if they do not pay immediately.

notes.he: בתחילת תביעת כתובתה להפסידה מזונותיה:
notes.en: Since we attended to her at the outset: at the start of her claim for her marriage contract, to make her lose her sustenance.

notes.he: להגבותה כתובתה:
notes.en: We attend to her in the end: to collect her marriage contract for her.

notes.he: כשתובעת כתובתה מזדקקין לה לבסוף ומגבינן לה כתובתה ובעי הכרזה:
notes.en: Since we attended to her at the outset, when she claims her marriage contract, we attend to her in the end and collect her marriage contract for her, and it needs a proclamation.

messages.text: In any case, the mishna poses a difficulty for the opinion of Rav Asi, who maintains that the court attends to the property of orphans only in order to collect the payment of a loan that accrues interest, not for the payment of a marriage contract. If the mishna is dealing with a gentile creditor, he will not wait thirty days to collect payment, and if it is referring to a Jewish creditor, he is prohibited from charging interest in the first place.

notes.he: דאמר אין נזקקין אלא לרבית ואין כאן רבית:
notes.en: In any case it is difficult for Rav Asi: who said one attends only for interest, and there is no interest here.

messages.text: Actually, the mishna is referring to a gentile creditor, in the specific case of one who accepted upon himself to adjudicate in accordance with Jewish law. He therefore agrees to delay collection for thirty days.

notes.he: דשקיל רבית ודקשיא לך פרסי מי ממתין על הכרזה שקבל עליו לדון להמתין על ההכרזה אבל נוטל רבית:
notes.en: Actually with a Persian creditor, who takes interest. And as for your difficulty, will a Persian wait for the proclamation: it is where he accepted upon himself to be judged, to wait for the proclamation, but he takes interest.

messages.text: If so, let him also not take interest, as it is prohibited to do so according to Jewish law.

The mishna is dealing with a case where he accepted Jewish law upon himself for this matter, to delay collection for thirty days, but he did not accept it upon himself for that matter, not to collect interest.
Come and hear a difficulty for the opinions of Rav Asi and Rabbi Yoḥanan from a mishna:
A court can collect a father’s debt from the property of orphans only from land of the lowest quality.

What are we dealing with in this mishna? If we say that the mishna is referring to a gentile creditor, will he comply and accept inferior-quality land as payment? Rather, it is obvious that we are dealing with a Jewish creditor.

notes.he: ואי כרב אסי דאמר משום רבית דקא אכיל ישראל ריבית מי שבקינן כו':
notes.en: Will a Persian comply and take inferior land? And if, like Rav Asi who said [one attends] because of interest, a Jew is consuming interest, do we let him, etc.

messages.text: Now, if the mishna is referring to a case where the interest consumes the orphans’ property, do we leave him to collect interest? Rather, it must be dealing with a case where the interest does not consume the orphans’ property, and yet it is taught in the mishna that the court attends to the property of orphans even when no interest accrues on the loan.

Once again: Granted, the mishna is not difficult according to the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, as he can establish it as referring to payment of the marriage contract of a wife. But according to the opinion of Rav Asi, that the court does not attend to the property of orphans in such a case, the mishna poses a difficulty.

notes.he: דכתובת אשה בזיבורית היא ומשום דקא מפסדא מזונות:
notes.en: Granted, according to Rabbi Yoḥanan it works out: since a wife’s marriage contract is from inferior land, and because she causes a loss through sustenance.

messages.text: Rav Asi could say to you: And according to the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, does the mishna work out well? If the mishna is referring to payment of a wife’s marriage contract, why does it discuss specifically a collection from orphans? Even in a case of a divorced woman who collects payment from the husband himself, she also receives only inferior-quality land.

notes.he: אפילו מיניה דידיה דבעל לא שקלה אלא זיבורית ומאי קמ"ל דיתמי:
notes.en: Even from the husband himself she takes only inferior land; so what does it teach us with orphans?

messages.text: This is not difficult, as Rabbi Yoḥanan would reply that the mishna is in accordance with the opinion of Rabbi Meir,
A marriage contract of a wife is generally paid with intermediate-quality land, and if payment is collected from orphans, the marriage contract is paid with inferior-quality land.

notes.dh: הא לא קשיא ר"מ היא דאמר כתובת [אשה] בבינונית
notes.he: מיניה דידיה כגון אם גירשה וקמ"ל דמיתמי בזיבורית:
notes.en: This is not difficult; it is Rabbi Meir, who says a wife’s marriage contract is from intermediate land: that is, from [the husband] himself, for example if he divorced her; and it teaches us that from orphans it is from inferior land.

notes.he: ר' יוחנן כר' מאיר סבירא ליה דמיניה דבעל בבינונית:
notes.en: This is not difficult: Rabbi Yoḥanan holds like Rabbi Meir, that from the husband [it is] from intermediate land.

messages.text: In any case, the mishna poses a difficulty for the opinion of Rav Asi.
Actually, the mishna is referring to a gentile creditor who accepted upon himself to adjudicate in accordance with Jewish law. He therefore agrees to accept payment from inferior-quality land.

notes.he: שקבל עליו בדיני ישראל למישקל מיתמי בזיבורית אבל נוטל רבית לפיכך נזקקין] על מנת ליתן לאשה כתובתה ולבעל חוב חובו בין מנכסי יתומים בין מנכסי הקדש וכגון שהקדיש נכסיו ומת והיתה עליו כתובת אשה זו ובע"ח זה [והיתומין צריכין לפדות הנכסים מן ההקדש ע"מ ליתן לאשה כתובתה כו':
notes.en: That he accepted upon himself, under Jewish law, to take from orphans from inferior land, but he takes interest; therefore one attends. In order to give the wife her marriage contract and the creditor his debt: whether from the property of orphans or from consecrated property, for example where he consecrated his property and died, and this wife’s marriage contract and this creditor were upon him, and the orphans need to redeem the property from the Temple treasury in order to give the wife her marriage contract, etc.

messages.text: If so, let him also not take interest, which is prohibited according to Jewish law.

The mishna is dealing with a case where he accepted Jewish law upon himself for this matter, to delay collection for thirty days, but he did not accept it upon himself for that matter, not to collect interest. The court therefore attends to the property of the orphans in order to minimize the interest owed to the creditor.
Come and hear a difficulty from a baraita:

When one proclaims the appraisal of the property of orphans, he announces that the property is being sold in order to give the proceeds to a wife as payment of her marriage contract or in order to give a creditor payment of his debt.

Granted, there is no difficulty in the ruling that one proclaims that the property is being sold in order to give a creditor payment of a debt, as whether according to this Sage or whether according to that Sage, i.e., Rav Asi or Rabbi Yoḥanan, the mishna is in accordance with that which we taught above, that it is dealing with a gentile creditor who collects interest but agrees to delay payment.

notes.he: בבעל חוב עובד כוכבים:
notes.en: As we answered: with a gentile creditor.

notes.he: לשטר שיש בו רבית דתרוייהו מודו דנזקקין לב"ח משום רבית] כשחייב מודה [קודם מיתתו שעדיין יש עליו כתובת אשה זו או חוב זה] וצוה לתת:
notes.en: Whether according to this Sage or according to that Sage, as we answered: for a document that contains interest, both agree that one attends to a creditor because of interest. When the one obligated admits before his death that this wife’s marriage contract or this debt is still upon him, and instructed to give it.

messages.text: But with regard to the proclamation that the property is being sold in order to pay the wife’s marriage contract, granted, according to the opinion of Rabbi Yoḥanan, who maintains that the court attends to the property of orphans in such a case, the baraita works out well. But according to the opinion of Rav Asi, that the court does not attend to their property in order to pay a marriage contract, the baraita poses a difficulty.

Here we are dealing with a case where the one who is obligated to pay admits that he has not yet paid, i.e., the father admitted before his death that he has not yet paid the obligation stated in the marriage contract.

notes.he: בשעת מיתה הודה אביהם:
notes.en: When the one obligated admits: their father admitted at the time of his death.

notes.he: וצוה לתת:
notes.en: When the one obligated admits, and instructed to give it.

messages.text: Now that you have arrived at this response, it is no longer necessary to establish that the previous cases are referring to a gentile creditor. Rather, all of them are also dealing with Jewish creditors, as they are referring to situations where the one who is obligated to pay admits that he has not yet paid. In such cases, the court collects payment from the property of the orphans without delay.

notes.he: ובעל חוב ישראל:
notes.en: All of them too, when the one obligated admits: and with a Jewish creditor.

notes.he: אותה ששנינו למעלה בב"ח פרסי לעולם בב"ח ישראל ואמאי נזקקין:
notes.en: All of them too: those we answered above as speaking of a Persian creditor are really with a Jewish creditor. And why does one attend?

messages.text: § With regard to the dispute between Rav Asi and Rabbi Yoḥanan, the Gemara relates that Mareimar collected the payment of a marriage contract for a divorced woman from the property of minor orphans.

notes.he: אין לה מזונות:
notes.en: A divorcée: she has no sustenance.

notes.he: שגירשה בעלה ומת:
notes.en: For a divorcée: whose husband divorced her and died.

messages.text: The daf’s text names Mareimar as the one who collected, and then has Ravina speak to Ameimar.

@Ameimar But doesn’t Rav Yehuda say that Rav Asi says that the court does not attend to the property of minor orphans unless interest was consuming it, and Rabbi Yoḥanan says that the court attends to their property either to pay a debt recorded in a promissory note that contains interest or to pay a wife’s marriage contract, due to the obligation of the orphans to provide her sustenance.
messages.quote: a marriage contract for a divorced woman from the property of minor orphans

notes.he: אע"ג דגרושה לית לה מזוני:
notes.en: From the property of orphans: even though a divorcée has no sustenance.

messages.text: And even Rabbi Yoḥanan says that they attend to the property of minor orphans only in the case of a widow, as she causes loss to their property due to the sustenance she receives until she collects payment of her marriage contract. But in the case of a divorced woman, who does not receive sustenance from their property, Rabbi Yoḥanan agrees that the court does not collect payment of her marriage contract until the orphans reach majority.

@Ravina We learned that this statement of Rabbi Yoḥanan, that the court attends to the property of minor orphans in order to collect the payment of a marriage contract, is for the sake of favor, i.e., the court collects payment of a wife’s marriage contract not due to the sustenance that consumes the property of the orphans, but in order that the wife will find favor in the eyes of men so that they will marry her. This reason is equally applicable in the cases of a widow and a divorced woman.

notes.he: דאמר כתובת אשה מגבינן מיתמי:
notes.en: That of Rabbi Yoḥanan: who said that a wife’s marriage contract is collected from orphans.

notes.he: כדי שימצאו האנשים חן בעיני הנשים וינשאו להן והלכך אפילו גרושה נמי:
notes.en: We teach it because of favor: so that the men will find favor in the eyes of the women and they will marry them. Therefore even a divorcée too.

notes.he: ההיא דר' יוחנן או לכתובת אשה אנן] משום חינא מתנינן לה כדי שידעו הנשים שיש להן כתובה מן היתומים אפילו כשיתגרשו נזקקין להן להגבותן כתובתן אע"ג דאין להן מזונות ויתרצו לבעליהן ולא יצערו אותן ומתוך כך ימצאו חן בעיני בעליהן הלכך מגבינן לגרושה משום חינא דכל הנשים:
notes.en: That of Rabbi Yoḥanan, “or for a wife’s marriage contract”: we teach it because of favor, so that women will know that they have a marriage contract from the orphans; even when they are divorced, one attends to them to collect their marriage contract, though they have no sustenance. And they will be agreeable to their husbands and not distress them, and through this they will find favor in their husbands’ eyes. Therefore we collect for a divorcée because of the favor of all women.

messages.text: At first, I would not attend to the property of orphans in order to collect payment of a standard debt. Once I heard that which Rav Huna, our friend, said in the name of Rav:
messages.lead: With regard to attending to the property of orphans:

notes.dh: אמר רב נחמן מריש לא הוה מזקיקינן ליתמי כו' מכאן ואילך מזקיקינן כו'
notes.he: והלכה כרב נחמן בדיני דנזקקין לנכסי יתומים והכי נמי איתא בהכותב (כתובות דף פד.) גבי הא דתנן מי שמת והניח אשה ובעל חוב ויורשים והיה לו מלוה או פקדון ביד אחרים ינתן לכושל שבהם ואמר ר' יוחנן עלה (שם) לכתובת אשה משום חינא אלמא נזקקין:
notes.en: Rav Naḥman said: At first I would not attend to orphans… from then on I would attend: The halakha follows Rav Naḥman in [matters of] law, that one attends to the property of orphans. And so too it is in the chapter HaKotev (Ketubot 84a), on what we learned: One who died and left a wife, a creditor and heirs, and he had a loan or a deposit in the hands of others, it is given to the weakest of them; and Rabbi Yoḥanan said about it: to the wife’s marriage contract, because of favor. Evidently one attends.

messages.text: Orphans who consume that which is not theirs, let them follow their deceased parent to the graveyard.

notes.he: ימותו כאביהם שהניח להם ממון זה:
notes.en: Let them go after those who left them: let them die like their father, who left them this money.

notes.he: כלומר שהיה מקללן שלא יאריכו ימים אלא ילכו אחר אביהן שהניחן למיתה הואיל ואוכלין שאינו שלהן:
notes.en: Let them go after those who left them: that is, he would curse them that they not live long but go after their father, who left them by dying, since they consume what is not theirs.

messages.text: From that point forward I would attend to their property.

notes.he: כדי למונען מאיסורא:
notes.en: I would attend: in order to keep them from a prohibition.

messages.text: At the outset, what is the reason that Rav Naḥman would not collect payment from minor orphans?
messages.quote: At first, I would not attend to the property of orphans

notes.he: הוה מזדקיק משום דרב פפא אמר פריעת כו':
notes.en: At the outset, what is the reason that he would not attend? Because Rav Pappa said: Repayment, etc.

messages.text: The repayment of a creditor is a mitzva, and minor orphans are not obligated in performing that mitzva.

notes.he: דקטנים הן אלא ימתין עד שיגדילו:
notes.en: They are not fit to perform a mitzva: since they are minors; rather, let him wait until they grow up.

messages.text: The reason is that we say there is a concern that the father might have transferred bundles of coins to the creditor before his death as collateral and we are unaware of such a payment. Therefore, the court delays payment until the orphans reach majority in order to allow them time to clarify whether such payment was in fact made.

notes.he: אביהם נתן לבעל חובו מעות או כסף וזהב במשכון בשעת מיתה ולא הספיק ליטול את השטר מידו:
notes.en: He placed bundles in his hand: their father gave his creditor coins, or silver and gold, as a pledge at the time of his death, and did not manage to take the document back from him.

notes.he: אימור צררי איתפסיה הלוה למלוה קודם מיתתו שיתפרע חובו מהן]:
notes.en: Say he placed bundles: the borrower placed [them with] the lender before his death, so that his debt would be repaid from them.

messages.text: What is the practical difference between these two explanations?

There is a practical difference between them in a case where the one who is obligated to pay admits that he still owes the money, or in a case where the court excommunicated the father in order to force him to pay and he died in a state of excommunication.

notes.he: ב"ד לאביהן על שאינו פורע לזה חובו ומת בשמתיה דהשתא ליכא למיחש לצררי דלא היה פורעו אלא בבית דין כדי שיתירו נידויו:
notes.en: Where they excommunicated him: the court [excommunicated] their father because he would not pay this man his debt, and he died in his excommunication. Now there is no need to worry about bundles, for he would have paid him only in court, so that they would lift his ban.

notes.he: בשעת מיתתו שעדיין חייב לו מאן דאמר משום מצוה לא פרעי דיתמי לאו בני מעבד מצוה נינהו ומאן דאמר משום צררי כיון דמודה ליכא למימר צררי אתפשיה:
notes.en: The difference between them is when the one obligated admits at the time of his death that he still owes him. According to the one who says it is because of a mitzva, they do not pay, since orphans are not fit to perform a mitzva; according to the one who says it is because of bundles, since he admits, one cannot say he placed bundles.

notes.he: שתפסו לדין] ושמתוה ב"ד ללוה [שיפרעם למלוה] ומית בשמתיה דהכא ודאי ליכא למימר צררי אתפשיה וחייבים היתומים לפרוע ולמאן דאמר משום מצוה לא פרעי:
notes.en: Or else: that they brought him to judgment and the court excommunicated the borrower to make him pay the lender, and he died in his excommunication. Here certainly one cannot say he placed bundles, and the orphans are obligated to pay; and according to the one who says it is because of a mitzva, they do not pay.

messages.text: In such instances, there is no doubt that the debt must be paid. According to Rav Pappa, even in such cases the court does not collect payment from minor orphans, as they are not obligated in the performance of the mitzva, whereas Rav Huna would rule that the court collects payment even before they reach majority, as there is no doubt that the debt is unpaid.

They sent from there, Eretz Yisrael, a communication that all these cases cited above, in which the court collects payment of a debt from the property of minor orphans, are referring to situations where the court excommunicated the father and he died while under excommunication. And the halakha is in accordance with the opinion of Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua.

notes.he: מיתוקמי כל הנך מתנייתא דלעיל דאמרו נזקקין:
notes.en: They sent from there: where they excommunicated him and he died in his excommunication. All those mishnayot above that said “one attends” are established [as speaking of this case].

notes.he: דהיכא דלא שמתוה חייש לצררי:
notes.en: And the halakha follows Rav Huna: that where they did not excommunicate him, one is concerned about bundles.

notes.he: מזדקקינן דהתם ודאי ליכא למיחש דצררי איתפשיה אבל בעלמא אפילו כשחייב מודה לא מזדקקינן דאיכא למימר מודה דחייב ליה אבל איכא למיחש דצררי [משכון] אתפשיה:
notes.en: They sent from there: where they excommunicated him and he died in his excommunication, we attend, for there certainly there is no need to worry that he placed bundles. But in general, even when the one obligated admits, we do not attend, since one can say that he admits he owes him, but there is a concern that he placed bundles [as a pledge].

notes.he: [והלכתא כרב הונא בריה דרב יהושע דאמר חיישינן לצררי:
notes.en: And the halakha follows Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, who said we are concerned about bundles.

messages.text: The Gemara attempts to determine the correct reason why the court does not attend to the property of minor orphans. We learned in the mishna:

One proclaims the appraisal of the property of minor orphans that is being sold for thirty days, and one proclaims the appraisal of consecrated property for sixty days, and one proclaims it in the morning and in the evening.

What are we dealing with here? If we say that the mishna is dealing with a gentile creditor who is unwilling to wait until the orphans reach majority, will he comply with the court’s directive that the appraisal of the property be proclaimed for thirty days before it is sold? Rather, it is obvious that the mishna is dealing with a Jewish creditor.

notes.he: דלא בעי למינטר עד דגדלי מי צאית להמתין ימי הכרזה:
notes.en: If we say with a gentile creditor: who does not want to wait until they grow up, will he comply and wait the days of proclamation?

messages.text: Granted, according to the opinion of Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, who says that the court does not attend to the property of minor orphans due to a concern that their father might have left bundles of coins with the creditor, he can establish the mishna as referring to a case where the one obligated to pay, i.e., the father, admits before his death that he has not paid. In such a case, the court does not wait to collect payment until the orphans reach majority.

notes.dh: בשלמא לרב הונא מוקים לה בשחייב מודה
notes.he: משום הכי מזדקקינן דלא אתפשי צררי:
notes.en: Granted, according to Rav Huna, he establishes it where the one obligated admits: that is why we attend, since he did not place bundles.

messages.text: But according to the opinion of Rav Pappa, that the court does not attend to the property of minor orphans because they are not obligated in the mitzva to repay a loan, the mishna poses a difficulty.

notes.he: דאמר יתמי לאו בני מעבד מצוה אמאי מזדקקינן:
notes.en: But according to Rav Pappa, who said orphans are not fit to perform a mitzva, why do we attend?

messages.text: Rav Pappa could say to you: If you wish, say that the mishna is referring to a case where the court sells the property of the orphans in order to collect payment for a marriage contract, which the court does for the sake of favor, i.e., in order that the wife will own property and be desirable for marriage.

And if you wish, say instead that the mishna is dealing with a gentile creditor who accepted upon himself to adjudicate in accordance with Jewish law. He therefore agrees to delay collection for thirty days.

notes.he: ומשום רבית וקביל עליו לדון בדיני ישראל להכרזה]:
notes.en: And if you wish, say with a Persian creditor: and because of interest; and he accepted upon himself to be judged by Jewish law regarding the proclamation.

messages.text: If he accepted Jewish law upon himself, then let him wait for the orphans until they reach majority before demanding payment of the loan.

The mishna is referring to a case where he accepted Jewish law upon himself for this matter, to delay collection for thirty days, but he did not accept it upon himself for that matter, to wait until they reach majority.
Come and hear a proof from a baraita:

notes.he: דתניא לעיל גבי הכרזה על מנת ליתן לאשה כו':
notes.en: Come and hear: what was taught above about the proclamation: “in order to give to a wife,” etc.

messages.text: When one proclaims the appraisal of the property of orphans, he announces that the property is being sold in order to give the proceeds to a wife as payment of her marriage contract, or in order to give a creditor payment of his debt.

What are we dealing with in the baraita? If we say that the baraita is referring to a gentile creditor who is unwilling to wait until the orphans reach majority, will he comply with the court’s directive that the appraisal of the property is proclaimed for thirty days before it is sold? Rather, it is obvious that the mishna is referring to a Jewish creditor.

notes.he: לימי הכרזה:
notes.en: Will he comply: with the days of proclamation?

messages.text: Granted, according to the opinion of Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, he can establish the mishna as referring to a case where the one obligated to pay admits before his death that he has not paid. But according to the opinion of Rav Pappa, granted, the court collects payment of a marriage contract for the sake of favor; but the fact that they sell the property in order to pay a creditor poses a difficulty.

Actually, the baraita is dealing with a gentile creditor, and it is referring to a case where he accepted upon himself to adjudicate in accordance with Jewish law. He therefore agrees to delay collection for thirty days.
If he accepted Jewish law upon himself, then let him wait for the orphans until they reach majority before demanding payment of the loan.

The baraita is dealing with a case where he accepted Jewish law upon himself for this matter, to delay collection for thirty days, but he did not accept it upon himself for that matter, to wait until they reach majority.

The court does not collect payment from the property of minor orphans due to the concern that there might be a receipt, i.e., perhaps their father repaid the loan and received a receipt attesting to his payment and the orphans are unaware of its existence.
messages.quote: At the outset, what is the reason that Rav Naḥman would not collect payment from minor orphans?

notes.he: הא דאין נזקקין לנכסי יתומין:
notes.en: Rava said: [the reason] that one does not attend to the property of orphans.

notes.he: דשמא שובר היה לאביהם על השטר הזה שפרעו ויתומים אין יודעין היכן הוא:
notes.en: Because of a receipt: perhaps their father had a receipt on this document, showing that he paid it, and the orphans do not know where it is.

notes.he: ואיכא בינייהו בין רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע דאמר משום צררי ובין רבא דאמר משום שובר היכא שמסר שטרותיו לאדם אחד בפני עדים ואמר דאין לו שום שטרות כי אם אותם שמסר לו דהשתא לשובר ליכא למיחש שהרי מסר כל שטרותיו לזה ואם איתא דהוה ליה שובר הוה מסר ליה אבל לצררי מ"מ איכא למיחש:
notes.en: Rava said: Because of a receipt. The difference between Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, who said because of bundles, and Rava, who said because of a receipt, is where [the father] handed his documents to one person before witnesses and said that he had no documents other than those he had handed him. Now there is no concern about a receipt, since he handed all his documents to this man, and had he had a receipt he would have handed it to him; but about bundles there is still a concern.

notes.he: לא הוה מיזדקיק רב נחמן מעיקרא דאיכא למימר שמא שובר היה ביד לוה שפרוע שטרו של מלוה ואבדו לפיכך אין נזקקין:
notes.en: Rava said, because of a receipt: Rav Naḥman did not attend at first, because one can say that perhaps the borrower had a receipt showing that the lender’s document was paid, and it was lost; therefore one does not attend.

messages.text: @Rava But are we concerned for the existence of a receipt? Didn’t we learn in a mishna:

notes.he: אמר ליה רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע לרבא ומי חיישינן לשובר והא תנן הנפרעת שלא בפניו כו' - ואי חיישינן לשובר הכא נמי ליחוש וא"ת רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע תקשי ליה נמי לנפשיה ליחוש לצררי וי"ל דהוה פשוט לרב הונא בריה דרב יהושע דמשום צררי אין למנוע לפרוע שלא בפניו משום שלא יהא כל אחד ואחד נוטל מעותיו של חבירו ויושב לו במדינת הים אבל משום חששא דשובר לא הוה מסיק אדעתא לומר כן ומשום הכי הקשה לו ליחוש לשובר ותירץ לו התם כדאמרי' שלא יהא כל אחד ואחד כו':
notes.en: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said to Rava: But are we concerned about a receipt? Didn’t we learn: One who collects in his absence…; and if we are concerned about a receipt, here too let us be concerned. And if you will say: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, should find it difficult for himself too: let us be concerned about bundles! One can say: it was plain to Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, that because of bundles one should not refuse to collect in his absence, so that not everyone will take his fellow’s money and settle overseas; but because of the concern about a receipt, it did not occur to him to say so. That is why he asked him, “Let us be concerned about a receipt,” and he answered him: There it is as we say, so that not everyone, etc.

messages.text: A woman who collects the payment of her marriage contract from the property of her husband when not in his presence, e.g., if her husband is overseas, may collect only by means of an oath that she has not yet received payment.

notes.he: כגון ששלח לה בעל גט ממדינת הים:
notes.en: One who collects in his absence: for example, where the husband sent her a bill of divorce from overseas.

messages.text: An incident came before Rabbi Yitzḥak Nappaḥa in Antioch, and he issued a ruling and said: They taught this halakha, that she may collect the payment of her marriage contract in her husband’s absence, only with regard to the wife’s marriage contract, for the sake of favor. But a creditor does not have the right to collect the debt that is owed to him in the debtor’s absence.

notes.he: דבית דין יורדין לנכסי אדם שלא בפניו אלא כתובת אשה משום חינא אבל בעל חוב ימתין עד שיחזור:
notes.en: They taught only: that the court goes down to a person’s property in his absence only for a wife’s marriage contract, because of favor; but a creditor must wait until he returns.

notes.he: דנאמנת בשבועה ולא חיישינן לשובר אלא כתובת אשה משום חינא:
notes.en: They taught only: that she is believed with an oath and we are not concerned about a receipt, only for a wife’s marriage contract, because of favor.

messages.text: Even a creditor may collect a payment by means of an oath in the debtor’s absence.

And if you are concerned for the existence of a receipt, then in that case there as well, where the obligated party is overseas, let us be concerned that he has in fact paid the debt and received a receipt.

notes.he: ואי חיישת לשובר התם נמי ניחוש בב"ח אמאי נפרע שלא בפניו בשבועה ניחוש שמא שובר יש לו ללוה:
notes.en: And if you are concerned about a receipt, there too let us be concerned: why does a creditor collect in his absence with an oath? Let us be concerned that perhaps the borrower has a receipt.

messages.text: @Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua In that case there, one is not concerned about the existence of a receipt, in accordance with the reason that we say: It is in order that there should not be a situation where every person will take the money of another and go and reside in a country overseas, to prevent the creditor from collecting the money from his property.

notes.he: בב"ח הנפרע שלא בפניו אמרינן לא חיישינן לשובר כדאמרי' טעמא אבל בעלמא חיישינן לשובר:
notes.en: He said to him: There, with a creditor who collects in his absence, we say we are not concerned about a receipt, for the reason we stated; but in general we are concerned about a receipt.

messages.text: § The halakha is that the court does not attend to the property of minor orphans in order to pay the debts owed by their father. But if their father said before his death: Give so-and-so the payment of my debt, the court attends to their property.

notes.he: אביהן תנו נזקקין:
notes.en: And if he said: [if] their father [said] “Give,” one attends.

notes.he: לכאורה פירוש תנו החוב והיינו כרב הונא בריה דרב יהושע דהיכא דחייב מודה נזקקין וצ"ע אמאי שבק לישנא דחייב מודה ושמא לכך נקט האי לישנא תנו דשייך בחוב ובמתנה דאם צוה אביהם ליתומים ליתן מתנה דנותנין אם צוה בתורת המחלק נכסיו מתנה בכולה או במקצתה ועשה קנין והכי נמי משמע קצת דבמתנה קמיירי מדקאמר שדה זו ומנה זו נזקקין לו:
notes.en: And if he said “Give,” one attends: Seemingly this means “give the debt,” and this is like Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, that where the one obligated admits, one attends. And this needs study: why did it leave the wording “the one obligated admits”? Perhaps it uses this wording “give” because it fits both a debt and a gift: if their father instructed the orphans to give a gift, they give it, if he instructed it as one who distributes his property as a gift, all of it or part of it, and made an act of acquisition. And it somewhat appears so too, that it speaks of a gift, since it says: “this field” and “this hundred,” one attends to him.

notes.he: ותימה פשיטא שאם אמר תנו נזקקין כיון שנתנה במתנה ואומר ר"י נזקקין (איצטריכא ליה) והא דנקט לישנא דתנו משום דמסיים ביה שדה זו ומנה זו דשייך ביה תנו ועוד איכא הודאה דלא סגי דלא אמר בהו תנו או אתם עדי כגון שהודה מעצמו (והא דאמרי') בפרק גט פשוט (ב"ב קעד:) שכיב מרע שאמר תנו מנה לפלוני אמר תנו נותנין לא אמר תנו אין נותנין אדם עשוי שלא להשביע את בניו אבל תבעוהו והודה אפילו בלא אתם עדי ולא אמר תנו נותנין דאין אדם משטה בשעת מיתה כדמוכח בשילהי פרק גט פשוט (בבא בתרא קעה:):
notes.en: And if he said “Give,” one attends: And it is puzzling: it is obvious that if he said “give,” one attends, since he gave it as a gift! And the Ri says: “one attends” was needed. It uses the wording “give” because it ends with “this field and this hundred,” to which “give” applies. Furthermore, there is an admission, which does not suffice unless he said “give” about them, or “you are my witnesses,” for example where he admitted on his own. (And what we say) in the chapter Get Pashut (Bava Batra 174b): A dangerously ill person who said, “Give a hundred to so-and-so”: if he said “give,” they give; if he did not say “give,” they do not give, since a person is apt [to say such things] so that his sons will not appear wealthy. But if they claimed from him and he admitted, even without “you are my witnesses” and without saying “give,” they give, since a person does not jest at the time of death, as is evident at the end of the chapter Get Pashut (Bava Batra 175b).

notes.he: ואם אמר אבי היתומים קודם מיתתו תנו לפלוני נזקקין ב"ד ונותנין:
notes.en: And if the orphans’ father said before his death, “Give to so-and-so,” the court attends and gives.

messages.text: Specifically, if the father said: Give this field to so-and-so, or: Give this one hundred dinars to so-and-so, then the court attends to their property to collect payment, and the court does not install a steward [apotropos] to negotiate with the creditor on their behalf.

notes.he: אם אמר תנו שדה זו לפלוני בחובו או מנה זו נזקקין ליתן לו ואין צריך להעמיד אפוטרופוס ליתומים על כך:
notes.en: This field and this hundred: if he said “Give this field to so-and-so for his debt,” or “this hundred,” one attends to give it to him, and there is no need to install a steward for the orphans over it.

notes.he: כיון דאמר שדה זו ומנה זו אין צריך להעמיד אפוטרופוס לידע אם פרע אם לאו ויש לו שובר ומעמידין האפוטרופוס לידע אם פרע אם לאו ויש לו שובר ויעמידו האפוטרופוס לבקש השובר בין חפצי המת או למצוא שום עדות התפסת צררי וא"ת כיון דאמר תנו אפי' אינו חייב כלום יתנו לו כיון דמצוה מחמת מיתה הוא ויהא מתנה בעלמא ויש לומר שהוא סבור להתחייב בשביל חובו ולא לשום מתנה הלכך אין לתת אותה אלא למי שמתחייב לו וכן משמע פרק גט פשוט (ב"ב קעד:) על ההיא שהבאתי לעיל אמר תנו קיימיה לשטריה אלמא דמשום שיודע לו כשאמר תנו כאילו נתקיים השטר אבל אם לא היה חייב לא היה נותן בתורת מתנה:
notes.en: And one does not install a steward: since he said “this field and this hundred,” there is no need to install a steward to find out whether he paid or not and has a receipt. [Otherwise] one installs the steward to find out whether he paid or not and has a receipt: they install the steward to look for the receipt among the dead man’s belongings, or to find some testimony that he placed bundles. And if you will say: since he said “give,” even if he owes nothing they should give it to him, since it is an instruction on account of death, and it would be a mere gift! One can say: he thinks he is obligated because of his debt, and not as any gift; therefore it is to be given only to one to whom he is obligated. And so it is evident in the chapter Get Pashut (Bava Batra 174b), about the case I cited above: [if] he said “give,” he has validated his document. Evidently, because he acknowledges him when he says “give,” it is as though the document were validated; but had he not been obligated, he would not give it as a gift.

notes.he: ואם אמר תנו שדה זו ומנה זו לפלוני נזקקין ואין מעמידין אפוטרופוס ליתומים על זה הדבר לדון עם המלוה דכיון דאמר בפירוש שדה זו ומנה זו נותנין אותה לו:
notes.en: And if he said, “Give this field and this hundred to so-and-so,” one attends and does not install a steward for the orphans in this matter to litigate with the lender; since he said explicitly “this field and this hundred,” they give it to him.

messages.text: If he said: Give a field to so-and-so, i.e., an unspecified field, or: Give one hundred dinars to so-and-so, i.e., unspecified dinars, then the court attends to the property of the orphans and they install a steward to act on their behalf, to ensure that the best fields remain in their possession.

notes.dh: שדה סתם ומנה סתם נזקקין ומעמידין אפוטרופוס
notes.he: ליתומין לברור להן חלק יפה ולהגבות את זה מן הזיבורית:
notes.en: A field unspecified and a hundred unspecified, one attends and installs a steward: for the orphans, to choose a good portion for them and collect for this man from the inferior land.

notes.he: [אבל אם אמר שדה סתם ומנה סתם נזקקין ומעמידין אפוטרופוס ליתומים שיטעון שמא לא אמר על שדה זו אלא על זו וידחהו לזיבורית:
notes.en: But if he said “a field” unspecified or “a hundred” unspecified, one attends and installs a steward for the orphans, who will argue that perhaps he did not mean this field but that one, and push him off to inferior land.

messages.text: In all of these cases where the father told his children before his death to give an item, the court attends to the property of the orphans and they install a steward to act on their behalf,
messages.lead: By contrast, the Sages of Neharde’a say:

notes.he: אפי' שדה זו ומנה זו נזקקין ומעמידין אפוטרופוס בר מנמצאת שאינה שלו דאין צריך אפוטרופוס אלא מיד מוציאין אותה מידם דאחזוקי סהדי המעידים על הגזילה בשקרי לא מחזקינן:
notes.en: In all of them: even “this field” and “this hundred,” one attends and installs a steward, except for a field found not to be his, where no steward is needed, but it is removed from them at once; for we do not presume that the witnesses who testify about the robbery are liars.

notes.dh: אמרי נהרדעי בכולהו נזקקין ומעמידין אפוטרופוס
notes.he: פירוש בכולהו שדה זו ומנה זו:
notes.en: The Nehardeans say: In all of them one attends and installs a steward. That is, in all of them: “this field” and “this hundred.”

notes.he: בכולהו מעמידין אפוטרופוס אפילו באומר שדה זו ומנה זו]:
notes.en: In all of them one installs a steward: even where he says “this field and this hundred.”

messages.text: except for a situation where a field is found in their possession with regard to which witnesses have testified that it is not their father’s, but is in fact stolen. In such a case, the stolen field is seized and returned to its owner without recourse to a steward, as we do not presume that witnesses are liars.

notes.he: אבל נמצאת ביד היתומים שדה אחת שלא היתה של אביהן אלא גזולה נזקקין להוציא גזילה מידם ואין צריך אפוטרופוס:
notes.en: But if a field is found in the orphans’ hands that was not their father’s but stolen, one attends to remove the stolen property from them, and no steward is needed.

notes.dh: אבל נמצאת שהיתה לו שדה שאינו שלו
notes.he: ואמר תנו לו שלא היתה של מת אלא של זה שצוה ליתנה לו ודאי נותנין לו אותה שלא היתה שלו אע"ג דאמר שדה סתם ואין מעמידין אפוטרופוס דכיון דאיכא עדים דאמרי שלא היתה שלו אלא של זה אין צריך אפוטרופוס דאחזוקי סהדי בשקרי דאמרי דשל זה היא לא מחזקינן:
notes.en: But if it is found that he had a field that is not his, and he said “Give it to him”: that it was not the dead man’s but this man’s, to whom he instructed it be given. Certainly they give him that field, which was not his, even though he said “a field” unspecified, and they do not install a steward. Since there are witnesses who say that it was not his but this man’s, no steward is needed, for we do not presume that witnesses who say it is this man’s are liars.

messages.text: Therefore, we do not attend to the property of minor orphans in order to repay a standard loan, as Rava says: The halakha is that the court does not attend to their property.

notes.dh: אמר רב אשי הלכך אזדקוקי כו' דאמר רבא הלכתא אין נזקקין
notes.he: פירוש בעלמא היכא דאיכא למיחש לצררי כמו מילתא דרב אסי אין נזקקין לנכסי יתומים ואי אזדקיקנא פירוש היכא דנזקקין כגון שדה זו ומנה זו דאמר רבא נזקקין ואין מעמידין אפוטרופוס בהא לא סבירא לן כרבא אלא מוקמינן אפוטרופוס דאמרי נהרדעי בכולהו נזקקין ומעמידין אפוטרופוס לבר מנמצאת שדה שאינה שלו דאחזוקי שיקרא לא מיזדקיקנא ואין צריך להעמיד אפוטרופוס וא"ת דבפרק הגוזל בתרא (ב"ק קיב. ושם) בר חמוה דרבי ירמיה טרק גלי באפיה דר' ירמיה אתא לקמיה דרבי אבא א"ל שלו תובע א"ל והא מייתינא סהדי דאחזקי בחיי אבוה [א"ל] וכי מקבלין עדות שלא בפני בעל דין ומ"ש משמעתין דהיכא דנמצאת שאינה שלו מזקיקין ומקבלין עדות אע"פ שהיתומים קטנים וי"ל דהתם מתחלה היתה של אביו דיתום כי נמי איכא סהדי דאחזיק אין לנו לקבל עדות זה ואין אחזוקי סהדי בשיקרא דשמא שום תנאי היה לאביו עמו להחזיק [אע"פ] שהוא שלו אבל בשמעתין דנמצאת שדה שאינה שלו שהעדים מעידים שגזלה הלכך לא מחזקינן סהדי בשקרי שמא לא גזלה אלא ודאי גזלה וליכא למימר שמא חזר ולקחה כיון דבגזילה בא לידו לא אמרינן שמא חזר ולקחה כי הדבר ברור שהאב גזלה ואינו של אביו ושפיר נקבל העדות דגזלה האב שלא בפני בעל דין כיון שהדבר ברור לנו שאין השדה של אביו וכן בהך דהגוזל בתרא (שם:) דקאמר רבי יהושע תנוק שתקף בעבדי אביו וירד לתוך שדה חברו ואמר שלי הוא אין אומרים לו המתן עד שיגדיל אלא מוציאין אותו מתחת ידו ומסיק הש"ס דהתם דמפקינן מיניה דלא קיימא אחזקה דאבוה משמע דאיכא מילי דמקבלין עדות שלא בפני בעל דין ולכך נראה דהיכא דחייב מודה ממלוה על פה דנזקקין ויעידו עדים ששמעו הודאת האב בפני ב"ד ויגבו משל היתומים החוב על פי העדות ולא אמר אין מקבלין עדות אלא בפני בעל דין כיון שהדבר ברור בלא שום גמגום שהודה האב דמי לנמצאת שאינה שלו ומיהו מדררא דממונא הבאה מחמת יתומים כי נמי ידעינן בברור שלא התפיסו צררי כל החוב הבא מחמת היתומים אין נזקקין כדאיתא פרק שור שנגח ארבעה וחמשה (ב"ק לט. ושם) דשור שהזיק פטור מטעם דאין נזקקין ופירש ר"י דלא שייך צררי ומכל מקום אין נזקקין דאין מקבלין עדות שלא בפני בעל דין:
notes.en: In brief: Rav Ashi means that in general, where there is a concern about bundles, as in Rav Asi’s statement, one does not attend to the property of orphans; and where one does attend, as with “this field and this hundred,” where Rava said one attends without a steward, we do not hold like Rava but install a steward, as the Nehardeans say, except for a field found not to be his, where no steward is needed since we do not presume that witnesses are liars. Question: in HaGozel Batra (Bava Kamma 112a), Rabbi Yirmeya’s brother-in-law shut the door in his face; Rabbi Abba said he was claiming what was his own, and when [Rabbi Yirmeya] said he would bring witnesses that he had held it in the father’s lifetime, Rabbi Abba said: Does one accept testimony not in the presence of the litigant? How is that different from our passage, where a field found not to be his is taken and the testimony accepted even though the orphans are minors? Answer: there it had originally been the orphan’s father’s, so even with witnesses that [Rabbi Yirmeya] held it, the testimony should not be accepted; and that is not presuming the witnesses are liars, since the father may have had some arrangement with him to hold it although it was the father’s. Here the witnesses testify that he stole it, so it was certainly stolen; we do not say that perhaps he later bought it, since it came to him by robbery, and so the testimony may be accepted in the litigant’s absence. So too in HaGozel Batra (Bava Kamma 112b), Rabbi Yehoshua says that a child who seized his father’s slaves, or went down into another’s field and said “It is mine,” is not told to wait until he grows up, and the Talmud concludes that it is taken from him because the father’s possession was never established: there are matters where testimony is accepted in the litigant’s absence. Therefore it seems that where the one obligated admitted an oral loan, one attends: witnesses testify before the court that they heard the father’s admission, and the debt is collected from the orphans on their testimony, since the admission is clear, like a field found not to be his. Still, with liability arising from the orphans themselves, even when we know clearly that no bundles were placed, one does not attend, as in the chapter Shor SheNagaḥ Arba’a VaḤamisha (Bava Kamma 39a), where an orphans’ ox that did damage is exempt because one does not attend; the Ri explained that bundles do not apply there, yet one does not attend because testimony is not accepted in the litigant’s absence. Open on Sefaria for the full text.

messages.text: And if we attend to their property, e.g., in a case where the father told his children to repay the debt, we install a steward to act on behalf of the orphans, as the Sages of Neharde’a say: In all of the cases, the court attends to the property of minor orphans and installs a steward, except for a situation where a field is found in their possession that is not the father’s, as we do not presume that witnesses are liars.

messages.caption: Rava, the Sages of Neharde’a and Rav Ashi: when the court attends to orphans’ property, and when it appoints a steward.
